text:
alex: FYI eu-west1 started a weird eviction chain ~10:05 UTC when we autoscaled spot nodes. several gpu pods got evicted in waves :eyes:

maria: ugh. symptoms? logs?

alex: FailedScheduling for new pods + lots of 'node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate' interleaved with 'Insufficient allocatable pods' from kube-scheduler. suspect packing + nic limits + mixed taints.

sam: can you paste a kubectl describe for one of the evicted pods and a node?

alex: sure — snippet:
```
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  10s (x6 over 2m)  default-scheduler  0/8 nodes are available: 5 Insufficient cpu, 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
node snippet:
```
Allocatable:
  cpu:  56
  memory:  225Gi
  pods:  110
  nvidia.com/gpu: 8
Taints: dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule
Annotations: node.kubernetes.io/eni-max-pods=58
```

lee: interesting — eni/eni-max-pods means NIC/pod density is cutting into available pod slots even though GPU resources exist. if pod requests many GPUs and high cpu, scheduler marks Insufficient pods.

priya: plus our spot nodepool had a taint `spot=true:PreferNoSchedule` and some workloads didn't tolerate it; autoscaler spun up a couple of spot racks then evictions started when on-demand drained.

infra-bot: @channel Detected surge: GPU eviction rate > 30% in eu-west1 for the last 12m. Suggested mitigations: enable podTopolgySpread relaxation, reduce per-pod hostPort usage, review taints.

maria: any evidence of topologySpread constraints making tight packing worse? we added a strict topologySpread for availability earlier this quarter.

alex: yes — many GPU jobs use topologySpreadAcrossNodes with maxSkew=1. that prevents consolidating onto fewer nodes when capacity is tight. combined with ENI pod limits it creates fragmentation.

sam: so pile of constraints = cpu+gpu+pods-per-node+topologySpread+taints -> scheduler can't place, falls back and evicts older pods. cascade.

lee: short-term fixes: 1) relax topologySpread policy to prefer rather than require 2) add a toleration for `spot=true` for batch jobs 3) bump node ENI max pods via custom AMI/enhanced networking where possible.

priya: longer-term: support a packing knob (we've been prototyping 'compactness' that trades availability skew for denser GPU packing) so batch workloads can opt into denser binpacking.

ops-oncall: rolling mitigation applied: relaxed topologySpread for gpu-batch namespace, added toleration to batch job controller, and scaled up on-demand pool by 2 nodes to absorb pressure. monitoring-ingress alert suppressed for now.

alex: thanks @ops-oncall. after mitigations eviction rate down to ~4% in last 5m. still seeing some pods Pending with 'node(s) had taints'.

sam: can we add a quick scheduler predicate test to simulate ENI limits? would help qualify changes before rollouts.

maria: I'm worried about cost if we keep on-demand buffer long-term. can we backfill with compactness-mode on spot nodes once stabilized?

priya: that's the plan. compactness-mode + a postscale job that reconciles packing after spikes. also evaluating per-node pod-density autoscaling (pack small GPUs on the high-density SKU).

alex: note: network egress seemed fine, this is almost exclusively placement/pod-count density. leaving this thread for follow-ups on compactness rollout and a postmortem draft. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment notice — patch that relaxes topologySpread was applied to `gpu-batch` namespace at 10:22 UTC (rollout: canary -> 100%).

ops-oncall: I'll open a short postmortem with timeline + recommended scheduler flags. tagging @maria @priya for follow-up decisions.

maria: thanks — also let's add a test in perf-suite that simulates node taints + ENI limits to catch this before next spike. :face_with_monocle:

alex: agree. closing for now, will link postmortem here when ready.
